title: Milestone Orchestration Playbook - Customer Implementation (Inference)
body:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a practical, engineer-friendly approach to tracking customer implementation milestones for inference rollouts. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), and partner SREs to coordinate ownership, surface blockers early, and align on renewal signals.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: GA+ inference features (hosted & dedicated). Covers discovery -> pilot -> go-live -> post-go-live optimization.
- Audience: CS leads, implementation PM, SE, SRE, customer POC.

High-level principles (quick):
- One source of truth: update the tracker at every sync (CS weekly, SE twice-weekly during pilot).
- Small milestones with clear owners (name + role) reduce ambiguity.
- Track blocker state, impact (P0/P1/P2), and mitigations alongside owner and ETA.
- Map rollout health to renewal signals (usage, latency, error rate, feature adoption).

Milestone taxonomy (recommended minimal set):
1) Kickoff & access provisioned (owner: CS Lead)
   - Deliverables: signed SOW/contract, access to sandbox account, security questionnaire received
   - Typical blockers: missing network allowlist, missing account owner, procurement delay
2) Integration PoC (owner: SE)
   - Deliverables: working end-to-end call to Redwood API or private endpoint, basic prompts validated
   - Typical blockers: incompatible prompt format, model variant mismatch, quota limits
3) Latency & throughput baseline (owner: SRE/SE)
   - Deliverables: p50/p95 latency, tokens/s throughput for target model under expected QPS
   - Typical blockers: network egress throttling, improper batching config, KV cache mis-use
4) Security & compliance signoff (owner: Customer Security + CS)
   - Deliverables: completed security checklist, KMS/HSM integration plan if needed
5) Pilot evaluation & quality gates (owner: SE + CS)
   - Deliverables: evaluation set, regression checks, human review feedback
   - Typical blockers: poor eval coverage, model hallucination cases without guardrails
6) Load/endurance test (owner: SRE)
   - Deliverables: sustained traffic run, autoscale validation, failure-mode tests
7) Go-live & traffic ramp (owner: CS + SRE)
   - Deliverables: go-live checklist complete, fallback routes defined, rollout schedule
8) Post-go-live optimization (owner: SE + Product)
   - Deliverables: token-cost optimizations, batching/caching recommendations implemented, quantization if applicable
9) Renewal/expand signal capture (owner: CS)
   - Deliverables: usage trends, satisfaction notes, QBR-ready slides

Suggested tracker columns (single-line CSV-friendly headings):
- milestone_id, milestone_name, owner_name, owner_role, target_date, status, percent_complete, last_update, blocker_state, blocker_description, blocker_impact, mitigation_plan, mitigation_owner, mitigation_eta, linked_tickets

Blocker lifecycle (practical):
- New -> Acknowledge (24h) -> Diagnose (48h) -> Fix plan (owner assigned) -> Mitigated -> Verified -> Closed
- Escalation path by impact:
  - P0: SE on-call + SRE + CS director (phone/Slack huddle)
  - P1: SE + SRE + CS manager (sync within 4 business hours)
  - P2: Track in weekly sync, no immediate escalation

Escalation email/Slack template (copy/paste):
- Subject: [P0] Customer X inference rollout blocker: network allowlist
- Body: Short summary, observed impact, steps attempted, immediate mitigation, owner + ETA, requested support

Communication cadence:
- Weekly CS sync with customer (status, blockers, actions). Owner: CS Lead.
- Bi-weekly technical touchpoint during integration/pilot (SE + SRE).
- Daily standup for first 72 hours after go-live for high-risk launches.
- QBR prep starts 30 days before renewal window; pull signals from tracker.

Renewal / expansion signals to capture from tracker:
- Sustained growth in tokens/month or active users over 12 weeks
- p95 latency consistently within committed SLA for 4 consecutive weeks
- % of calls using latest safety/guardrail hooks > 90% (if applicable)
- Quality verdict: human eval pass rate >= target threshold
- Integration maturity: authed production key in place, SRE runbooks created

Playbook templates (copyable snippets):
- Sprint-lane note for CS weekly sync:
  - Top 3 milestones (commitments this week)
  - Top 3 risks / blockers (impact and owner)
  - Help needed from internal team (who and why)
- Handoff checklist for SRE/Support after go-live:
  - Runbook link(s) shared, escalation contacts listed, alerting thresholds set, on-call rotation assigned

Metrics to maintain in tracker (minimum):
- Implementation velocity: % milestones completed on time (rolling 8-week window)
- Time-to-first-successful-inference (TTFSI): hours from kickoff to first successful prod inference
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for P0/P1 blockers
- Customer satisfaction note (text) after pilot

Example (small sample row):
- 003, Latency baseline, Ravi Patel, SRE, 2026-01-21, at_risk, 60%, 2026-01-16, blocked, egress throttling from customer VPC, P1 - impacts p95, SE attempted config change, mitigation plan: open network tunnel + increase egress quota, mitigation_owner: SolutionsEng-Team, mitigation_eta: 2026-01-19, linked_tickets: JIRA-IS-4321

Operational tips and gotchas (from past rollouts):
- Don’t assume customer-side load balancers preserve source IP for rate-limiting; this can hide burst patterns.
- Autoscale can mask cold-start latency; capture cold-start tail separately in early testing.
- For private deployments, align on KMS responsibilities early — customers often underestimate HSM procurement timelines.
- Keep a short list of model-fallbacks (lighter quantized variant, CPU fallback) to reduce downtime risk during capacity constraints.

Unresolved questions / TODOs for the playbook (working list):
- Finalize mapping of tracker health states to renewal probability (sales data needed).
- Add a templated Sparksheet that the CS rep can drop into a QBR slide deck (need comms/design help).
- Surface more concrete checklists for Dedicated vs Hosted differences (SLA thresholds, config knobs).

Quick start: How to use this doc in practice
1) At kickoff, CS creates a tracker row per milestone above, assigns an owner, and commits dates.
2) SE fills integration acceptance criteria inline with the milestone row.
3) SRE runs baseline tests and populates latency/throughput results in the tracker.
4) CS updates renewal signals and flags QBR slides 30 days out.

Notes to self (informal):
- Consider adding a lightweight Airtable template for customers who want a shared editable view.
- Add an internal shortcut: /tracker new-milestone command in Slack to pre-populate a row (engineering partner needed).

Contact for feedback: Dana Rodriguez (CS Lead) — dana@redwood.ai
